solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bike on call for several nights at the opera

indicators.note: in an across clue, one word on another means it comes after it

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: Someone cycles off to the opera house for a run of several evenings' performances.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring cycle is four operas performed on separate nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's tetralogy of operas is normally staged over four evenings, hence several nights.

clue.text: Batter sections in defensive earthworks

parts.note: to batter is to ram, as with a battering ram
sections are parts

explanation.surface: Battering-ram crews attack sections of a castle's earthen defences.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramparts are the raised banks of earth built around forts and towns for protection.

clue.text: Spaniard rises for cursory greeting

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters of the word read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a Don is a Spanish gentleman

explanation.surface: A Spaniard stands up and offers a quick hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief tilt of the head is a casual acknowledgement given in passing.

clue.text: Copper diffident, not demanding

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
diffident means shy

explanation.surface: A timid police officer is no trouble to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is an easy one, requiring little effort.

clue.text: This team shouldn't chuck stones about?

definitions.text: This team shouldn't chuck stones about?

parts.words: This team shouldn't chuck stones about
parts.note: people in glass houses shouldn't throw stones, and this football club is named after a famous glass building

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says people in glass houses shouldn't throw stones; a London football club takes its name from the great glass exhibition hall of 1851.
explanation.definitionFit: The London football club is named after a huge glass-and-iron exhibition building, so the proverb about glass houses applies.

clue.text: Give reasons for maybe one dumped on prairie

indicators.note: in a down clue, one word on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, perhaps one who has been dumped
a prairie is a plain

explanation.surface: Someone jilted out on the open grassland wants to know why.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to account for it by setting out its causes.

clue.text: Charlie Bishop fed with old loaf

indicators.note: being fed with something means taking it inside, so one letter goes into the pair

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop called Charlie is given an old loaf to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a round, crusty kind of bread loaf.

clue.text: Be honest, what do you do in the shower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to confess the truth

definitions.text: what do you do in the shower
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: you emerge washed

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally: after a shower you come out clean.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to own up fully; read literally it describes leaving a wash spotless.

clue.text: British plead to sunbathe

parts.note: to plead is to ask

explanation.surface: A Briton begs to be allowed to lie in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask is to lie lazily enjoying warmth, especially sunshine.

clue.text: Humility in dirty place, after a fashion

indicators.note: one part placed after another, so the dirty place comes second

parts.note: a mode is a fashion
a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy place

explanation.surface: Someone shows humility by living in a pigsty, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a fashion' looks like a phrase meaning 'sort of'; split it so 'after' places the pieces and 'a fashion' is MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is the quality of not boasting about oneself, which is humility.

clue.text: Little pets stealing half of my footwear

indicators.note: the pups take the letter in, so it goes inside them

parts.note: pups are young dogs, little pets

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word means its first letter

parts.note: the word my

explanation.surface: Puppies have run off with some of my shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light, flat shoes, such as plimsolls or dancing shoes.

clue.text: Cornered by the sea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trapped and facing an attacker
second meaning: located at a bay on the coast

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read once as the idiom for a trapped quarry and once literally as being at a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunted animal held at bay is trapped; literally, being at a bay means on the coast.

clue.text: Seasonal song in plain setting, one from The Gondoliers?

indicators.note: the song goes in the plain word
the plain word acts as a setting around the song

parts.note: plain means bare, unadorned
a carol is a Christmas song

explanation.surface: A Christmas song, simply arranged, sounds like something from the Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gondoliers is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the question mark signals the answer is a gondolier's song, not a number from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian boating song traditionally sung by gondoliers.

clue.text: A particular church's unusual roofing?

parts.note: 'that' singles out a particular thing

explanation.surface: One specific church has an odd sort of roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed roofs are rare on modern buildings, so this covering counts as uncommon.

clue.text: Famous divorce centre — wife coming to bad end

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces

indicators.note: bad means the letters of the word end are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A marriage ends badly at a well-known divorce centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divorce centre' looks like the middle of a word; it is Reno, the Nevada city once known for quick divorces. 'Bad' turns END into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone renowned is widely known and celebrated, which is famous.

clue.text: Ignore foul: undeniable try

indicators.note: foul suggests the letters are messed up and reordered

explanation.surface: A rugby referee lets an obvious foul pass when an undeniable try is scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' reads as the offence to be ignored; it is the anagram signal for UNDENIABLE plus TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deliberately overlooking something you know is wrong.

clue.text: Strong flavour eased in cooking

indicators.note: cooking letters means mixing them up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A powerful taste is softened during cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise seed has a pungent liquorice taste used in sweets, drinks and baking.

clue.text: A small month in a yacht basin

parts.note: MAR is the short form of March

explanation.surface: A short month spent in a harbour for yachts.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a purpose-built harbour with moorings for pleasure boats.

clue.text: Fly around circle in dance

indicators.note: turned around means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: An insect buzzes round in circles as if dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a Latin American ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Carry minute family emblem

parts.note: to tote is to carry

explanation.surface: Someone carries a tiny family crest about.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal adopted as the symbol of a clan or kin group.

clue.text: Change hands over

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Instruction to switch hands, as in a sport or game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change hands' looks like one phrase; split it after 'Change'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: Entire? With gap

parts.note: a hole is a gap

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is the joke: something with a gap seems anything but complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Craftsman's painting is given a name

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A craftsman's picture gets a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand.

clue.text: At which one is confused, in the main?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the main is a poetic word for the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' means confused; 'the main' is an old word for the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is called the main in poetry, and being at sea is idiom for bewilderment.

clue.text: Something cooked, right off the jetty

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Something being cooked falls right off the jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish of pastry with a filling.

clue.text: Paradise where, having died, alderman transported

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An alderman who has died is carried off to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests rapture or the soul carried away; it rearranges ALDERMAN into REAMLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is an ideal, imaginary world, a kind of paradise.
